name: fortinet-fortisiemv2
label: Fortinet FortiSIEM v2
description: FortiSIEM v2 provides integrations that allow you to query and make changes to the CMDB, query events, and send incident notifications. This revamped connector adds async operations, MCP (Model Context Protocol) investigation tools, and native ingestion support, along with actions like get incidents, comment incident, clear incident, get device details, get monitored organizations, report-related actions, and get all associated events for an incident from FortiSIEM.

operations.description: Searches for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server based on search attributes and other input parameters you have specified.

parameters.title: Search Attributes
parameters.tooltip: Select one or multiple search attributes to prepare your search query
parameters.description: Select attribute types using which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. You can choose one or more search attributes from the following options: Destination Port, Destination IP, Event ID, Event Action, Incident ID, File Name, Host Name, Organization Name, Process Name, Post-NAT Source IP, Raw Event Log, Relay IP, Reporting Ip, Source IP, Source Port, Source MAC, or User If you choose Destination Port, then in the Destination Port IN field, enter the value of the destination port for which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Destination IP, then in the Destination IP IN field, enter a comma-separated list of destination IPs based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Event ID, then in the Event ID IN field, enter the value of the event ID for which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Event Action, then from the Event Action IN drop-down list, choose the event action for which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. You can choose 1-Deny or 0-Permit. If you choose Incident ID, then in the Incident ID IN field, enter the value of the Incident ID for which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose File Name, then in the File Name CONTAINS field, enter the name of the file based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Host Name, then in the Host Name CONTAINS field, enter the name of the host using which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Organization Name, then in the Organization Name CONTAINS field, enter the name of the organization based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Process Name, then in the Process Name CONTAINS field, enter the name of the process based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Post-NAT Source IP, then in the Post-NAT Source IP IN field, enter the Post-NAT source IP based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Raw Event Log, then in the Raw Event Log CONTAINS field, enter the search attribute for the raw event based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Relay IP, then in the Relay IP IN field, enter the relay IP based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Reporting IP, then in the Reporting IP IN field, enter the reporting IP based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Source IP, then in the Source IP IN field, enter the source IP based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Source Port, then in the Source Port IN field, enter the source port based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose Source MAC, then in the Source MAC CONTAINS field, enter the search attribute for the source MAC using which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server. If you choose User, then in the User CONTAINS field, enter the search attribute for the user based on which you want to search for events in the Fortinet FortiSIEM server.

parameters.tooltip: Specify a CSV list of incident IDs to be added to the case you want to update in FortiSIEM. Note: An incident ID can be assigned to only one case at a time, not multiple cases. This is an append operation and does not overwrite or remove any previously added incident IDs.
parameters.description: Specify a CSV list of incident IDs to be added to the case you want to update in FortiSIEM. Note: An incident ID can be assigned to only one case at a time, not multiple cases. This is an append operation and does not overwrite or remove any previously added incident IDs.

parameters.name: note
parameters.tooltip: Specify the note that you want to add to the case you want to update in FortiSIEM.  Note: This is an append operation that adds a new note without modifying existing ones.
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the note that you want to add to the case you want to update in FortiSIEM.  Note: This is an append operation that adds a new note without modifying existing ones.

operations.title: Get Case Analysts
operations.description: Retrieving a list of analysts from the FortiSIEM.

parameters.title: Organization
parameters.name: organization
parameters.tooltip: Specify the organization name to retrieve a list of case analysts from FortiSIEM. Note: This parameter is mandatory in Service Provider mode and optional in Enterprise mode.
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the organization name to retrieve a list of case analysts from FortiSIEM. Note: This parameter is mandatory in Service Provider mode and optional in Enterprise mode.

parameters.title: Time From
parameters.name: timeFrom
parameters.tooltip: Select the start time range to fetch the case analyst list from FortiSIEM. Note: You can specify a maximum of 90 days. If left blank, the default is 30 days.
parameters.description: (Optional) Select the start time range to fetch the case analyst list from FortiSIEM. Note: You can specify a maximum of 90 days. If left blank, the default is 30 days.

parameters.title: Time To
parameters.name: timeTo
parameters.tooltip: Select the end time range to fetch the case analyst list from FortiSIEM.
parameters.description: (Optional) Select the end time range to fetch the case analyst list from FortiSIEM.

parameters.title: Offset
parameters.name: start
parameters.tooltip: Specify the index of the first item to be returned by this operation. This parameter is useful for retrieving a subset of analysts, such as starting from the 10th analyst. By default, this is set as 0.
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the index of the first item to be returned by this operation. This parameter is useful for retrieving a subset of analysts, such as starting from the 10th analyst. By default, this is set as 0.

parameters.title: Limit
parameters.name: size
parameters.tooltip: Specify the maximum number of results this operation should return per page. The default is 100.
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the maximum number of results this operation should return per page. The default is 100.
